consumesExternalOutput.program: src/gates/gate-classes.ts, run as a gate subprocess, whose stdout and GateResult record the named test ingests
consumesExternalOutput.provenance: A SPEC'S MEMBERS MUST REDDEN EVERY TEST IT NAMES, not merely one of them: src/witness/run.ts:932 computes a run as red only when the exit code is nonzero AND failed.length === tests.length. The first version of this witness named both class tests in one spec and was correctly rejected, because narrowing the status vocabulary cannot reach a test that only uses `gates`. So the schema is covered by two specs of one test each rather than one spec of two, and that is a property of the harness rather than a preference. The capture is verbatim stdout of the gate under test, taken on 2026-09-17 against this branch over byte COPIES of two real phase declarations; the named test reads its asserted detail sentences out of it rather than carrying hand-written strings. Rule (f) does not bind this spec, because its members touch only the schema document and the spawn derivation does not match that file; the declaration is made anyway because the test DOES assert on another program's captured output. THE TWO MEMBERS ARE STRUCTURALLY DIFFERENT: the first RENAMES the whole gateClasses property so `additionalProperties: false` rejects every declaration carrying the field, and the second changes the TYPE of the `gates` list inside one class disposition, which leaves the field legal and makes the value illegal. One is about the property existing, the other about what it may hold.
